_about: Explain's checks after the model, before anything is spoken (backend/llm/natlas_guard.py): an answer naming a medicine, or using a dose word, is never spoken; the page is read instead. Medicine names are the same in every language; dose words are per language. In a dose word, N stands for a number: digits (4, 0.5), a number word of that language (content/number_words/) or a range ('4 to 6', '4-6'); a hyphen may be there or not ('4-hourly', '4 hourly'). DRAFT: for Dr. Amos to review and extend.

dose_abbreviations._about: Short dose words that are also ordinary words or letters ('bid', 'stat', 'daily', 'od', 'mane' as in a lion's mane). Each counts as a dose word only as a whole word right next to a number or a dose form ('1 tab bd', '500 mg tds', 'od x 5 days', 'bd for 7 days'), never on its own, so 'a bid to win' or 'daily life' is not blocked. DRAFT, for Dr. Amos.

dose_forms._about: Dose forms that make a short dose word count ('2 tabs bd'). Units are matched glued to a number too ('500mg tds').
